findings.title: A double click that opens a reading list picks or ticks whatever row the open scrolled under the pointer
findings.state_task_viewport: 373x410 DPR 1.5. Mouse user clicks a reading search box, or the 'Pick another reading' status button, with a normal double click (two presses about 90 ms apart) or a second click about 350 ms later. Cases: dial-configured and dial-groups with the rotation search at viewport y 344 (where it sits after a person scrolls to it); key-missing 'Pick another reading'; key-configured primary search at page top; key-details detail search at y 340.
findings.observed: MEASURED. The first press opens the list and the page jumps: revealOpenList (pi-common.js:2830) runs from mousedown (2914 and 2896), and reveal() (pi-shell.js:386) does the same for 'Pick another reading'. The second press, at the same point, lands on a list row. Combobox rows commit on mousedown, and checklist rows are native labels. Results per case: rotation checklist scrolled 44 to 156 and ticked 'CPU CCD1 (Tdie)' into the rotation (baseline: no scroll, 0 writes). 'Pick another reading' scrolled 0 to 261 and replaced the saved missing reading with CPU (Tctl/Tdie), 1 write (baseline: the pointer landed on a summary, 0 writes). Key primary picker scrolled 0 to 100 and picked CPU CCD1, in both builds. Detail checklist scrolled about 232 and the second press toggled a tile's size (1 detailTiles write), in both builds.
findings.evidence: MEASURED hw-r3y-power/p2-cand.json and p2-cand-rerun.json (fresh browser, identical), p2-base.json, p9-cand.json and p9-cand-rerun.json vs p9-base.json (pickDbl), p6-cand.json and p6-base.json (detailDbl). READ pi-common.js:2830-2842, 2896, 2914, 3007-3019 (row commit on mousedown); pi-shell.js:386-406.
findings.affected_user: Mouse users who double click, or click again right after opening (everyone at some point). The key-missing case hits the recovery flow.
findings.correction: After any page scroll the panel makes on a pointer open or a reveal, swallow the next press at the same client point (within 4 px) until the pointer moves or 500 ms pass. One document capture listener for mousedown and click, with preventDefault and stopPropagation, covers rows, labels and tile buttons alike. Alternative: on pointer opens, do not scroll the page; cap the list's height to the space below the field instead.
findings.tradeoff: A deliberate press made within 500 ms of the jump without moving the pointer is ignored once. Keyboard opens are unaffected. The alternative shows fewer rows on low fields.
findings.acceptance_test: At 373x410 DPR 1.5, send a CDP double click (clickCount 1 then 2, 90 ms apart) and a 350 ms second click on each case above: dial-configured rotation search at y 344, key-missing 'Pick another reading', key-configured primary search, key-details detail search at y 340. Each writes 0 settings, the list still opens, and the R17 e2e reach check still passes.
findings.register_ref: R17 (side effect); first pass missed the pre-existing primary and detail variants

findings.title: Holding Enter confirms an armed remove, Merge or Replace: the 450 ms guard is shorter than the key-repeat delay
findings.state_task_viewport: 373x410. dial-configured with three Elite groups; key-configured with Advanced > Config open. Keyboard user presses Enter on group 1's remove button (or on Merge, or on Replace shared settings) and holds it slightly longer than a tap.
findings.observed: MEASURED. With CDP keyDown autoRepeat events every 33 ms after 500 ms: a 560 ms hold removed group 1 and its readings (1 write). A 900 ms hold on Merge merged the groups and dropped their names (1 write). A 900 ms hold on Replace shared settings wrote the shared settings (1 global write). The first keydown arms; the first repeat arrives after 450 ms (armPress, pi-common.js:719; apply, 4768) and confirms. Windows' default repeat delay is about 500 ms and can be set to 250 ms (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: MEASURED hw-r3y-power/p3-cand.json T5_holdEnter; p4-cand.json merge_holdEnter, replace_holdEnter, remove_hold560. READ pi-common.js:718-742 and 4750-4770.
findings.affected_user: Keyboard users, users with motor tremor or slow key release, and screen reader users who press and hold
findings.correction: In the confirm branch, require a fresh press: ignore activations that come from repeated keydowns. On these buttons, preventDefault a keydown with ev.repeat, or require a keyup after arming before a confirm counts. Keep the 450 ms guard for double clicks.
findings.tradeoff: A person who deliberately holds Enter must release and press again, which is the intent of arm-then-confirm.
findings.acceptance_test: Focus group 1's remove, send keyDown Enter, then autoRepeat keyDowns every 33 ms for 2 s, then keyUp: 0 writes, button still armed. One more Enter press: exactly 1 write. Same for Merge with named groups and for Replace shared settings (0 global writes on the hold).

findings.title: The folded Controls summary hides a destructive reset reach
findings.state_task_viewport: 373x410, dial-configured. Legacy with 'A stats reset clears' set to 'Every dial, everywhere' (or 'The whole rotation set'); Elite with the same. Controls folded, which is its usual state.
findings.observed: MEASURED. Folded summary: 'Legacy: turn cycles readings · push resets session stats · tap cycles the stat'. The open list says 'Push: resets session stats (every dial, everywhere)'. On Elite the long push, which does the reset, is not in the summary at all. A Legacy push fires on dial down and resets every dial's session stats (READ src/controls.ts LEGACY.shortPress resetStats; sensor-dial.ts executeStateCommand with parseResetScope).
findings.evidence: MEASURED hw-r3y-power/p7-cand.json summary.legacy-all, legacy-set, elite-all (the summary, plus 'now' for the open list). READ pi-model.js:241. Raised as an S2 new concern in agents/x1/power.json; absent from REGISTER.md, so it is neither KEEP nor DEFER.
findings.affected_user: Power users who set a wide reset scope, and anyone reading the folded summary on a shared setup
findings.correction: When resetScope is 'set' or 'all', add the reach to whichever push resets: 'push resets stats on every dial' or 'long push resets the whole set'. Pay for it by dropping '(auto cycle is off)' from the pause clause when the reset clause is present.
findings.tradeoff: Can add a line to the folded row on those dials. The summary strings in test/pi-model.test.ts change.
findings.acceptance_test: dial-configured Legacy with resetScope 'all': the folded summary contains 'every dial'. Elite with 'all': it names the long push's reach. With 'current' the text is unchanged from today. 0 writes.

findings.title: A rotation rebuild silently disarms an armed group remove or Merge; on an auto-cycling dial the confirm window is at most one cycle
findings.state_task_viewport: 373x410, dial-configured Elite with three groups. Arm group 2's remove, then the dial moves (a readingKey echo, as an auto cycle step every 5 s or a hand turn produces), then press again.
findings.observed: MEASURED. After the echo, onSelectionEcho (pi-common.js:3117) rebuilds the headers. The button reads '×' again (armed unset) and keeps focus, while the live region still says 'Press again to remove group 2 and its 2 readings.' The second press at the same point only arms again: 0 writes. With auto cycle at its shortest (5 s), a confirmation has to land between 450 ms after arming and the next step, anywhere from 0 to 5 s. That is the timed window R09 removed from Replace because the spoken prompt alone takes about 5 s.
findings.evidence: MEASURED hw-r3y-power/p3-cand.json T6_armThenEcho. READ pi-common.js:943-1030 (renderRotationSet rebuilds every header on echo), 718-742 (arm state lives on the button element).
findings.affected_user: Screen reader and slower users removing a populated group on an auto-cycling or turning dial
findings.correction: Keep the arm in module state (group index plus a signature of its keys) and re-apply it in groupHeader when the same group is rebuilt. Clear it on blur, on any edit to that group, and on an index shift. Or update the 'on dial' badge in place on selection echoes instead of rebuilding the headers.
findings.tradeoff: An arm that survives rebuilds needs a clear invalidation rule, or a stale arm could confirm on a different group after a reorder.
findings.acceptance_test: Arm group 2's remove, send two readingKey echoes 1 s apart, press again 3 s after arming: exactly one write, removing group 2. Blur still disarms. After a group above is removed, the arm does not carry over to another group.

findings.title: The derived groups line promises group jumps while groups are not in effect
findings.state_task_viewport: 373x410. dial-configured Elite, press 'Split into groups' (group 1 holds all three readings, group 2 is empty). Also Custom with Touch zones 'Two' and Tap set to 'Switch sensor or group'. Task: read what a turn and a pressed turn do.
findings.observed: MEASURED. After Split, #rotation-help reads 'New ticks go to the marked group. Turns stay inside a group; a pressed turn jumps to the next group and shows its name.' The note under it reads '2 groups. They take effect once two of them hold readings; until then rotation runs as one flat list.' The folded Controls summary reads 'pressed turn switches sensor'. At runtime rotationGroupsOf returns undefined with fewer than two populated groups, so the flat set steps and a pressed turn switches sensors (READ rotation.ts:92-126, sensor-dial.ts:527-540). Custom with two zones and Tap = Switch: the line says 'a tap jumps to the next group', but with two zones every tap is a side (tapZoneOf) and scheme.tap never runs. Minor: Legacy with Ignore turns says 'turns run through all groups as one list' while the picker help says 'Turns are ignored here.'
findings.evidence: MEASURED hw-r3y-power/p1-cand.json A_afterSplit, I_onePopulated, E_twoZonesTapGroup, B_legacyIgnore; screenshot shot-split-contradiction-373.png. READ pi-common.js:836-880 (groupJumpers from preset only), pi-model.js groupsActive (used by the summary, not by this line), src/gestures.ts tapZoneOf.
findings.affected_user: Power users building groups (Split is the entry point every one of them passes through), and beginners reading the groups line
findings.correction: Emit the 'stay inside / jumps' sentence only when model.groupsActive(settings) is true; otherwise leave it to the note. Count Tap as a jumper only when touchZones is 'off' or 'three'. Say 'Turns are ignored' instead of 'turns run through' when rotationDisabled is on. Separately, for the owner: schemeCanSwitchGroups ignores touch zones, so a two-zone Tap = Switch dial is confined to one group with no way out.
findings.tradeoff: The line changes the moment group 2 gets its first reading. That is a render, not an announcement, so no chatter.
findings.acceptance_test: dial-configured Elite, Split: #rotation-help contains neither 'jumps' nor 'stay inside'. Tick one reading into group 2: the sentence appears in the same render. Custom, zones two, gestureTap stepGroup: no 'a tap jumps'. 0 writes from rendering.

findings.title: Twin tags fail for identical hardware: the same instance mark, or a long shared model name, yields identical tags
findings.state_task_viewport: 373x410 and 189x410, dial-configured. Rotation holds 'CPU Die (average)' from two sensors named 'CPU [#0]: Example 16-Core Processor: Enhanced' and '...: DTS' (the fixture's own naming style). Also two drives named 'S.M.A.R.T.: Samsung SSD 990 PRO 2TB (<serial>)'. Task: pick the right one to reorder or remove.
findings.observed: MEASURED. Both CPU chips read 'CPU Die (average) | #0'. Both drive chips read 'Drive Temperature | Samsung SSD 9…'. The visible text is identical; only title and sr-only text differ. twinTagOf (pi-common.js:418) takes the [#N] mark whenever one exists, else truncates the tail after the last colon to 13 characters, so the part that actually differs (DTS vs Enhanced, the serial) is dropped. INFERRED: HWiNFO names Intel DTS and Enhanced sensors under the same [#0], and S.M.A.R.T. sensors as 'model (serial)'.
findings.evidence: MEASURED hw-r3y-power/p7-cand.json twin; p7b-cand.json chips; screenshot shot-twins-smart-373.png.
findings.affected_user: Power users with identical drives or GPUs, or Intel CPUs (DTS and Enhanced both carry package and core readings); sighted users (screen readers get the full sensor)
findings.correction: Derive the tag from what differs among the colliding members: the [#N] mark only when the marks differ; else the last colon segment when it differs; else the shortest distinguishing end of the sensor name (for example the serial's last 4 to 6 characters); else HWiNFO's 1-based sensor order.
findings.tradeoff: Tags vary in style between cases, and a serial fragment means little to a beginner. The tooltip still carries the full name.
findings.acceptance_test: With the two added sensor pairs above, at 373 and 189: the two chips in each pair show different visible tags; unique names show no tag; the detail tile editor and Reading colors rows follow the same rule; 0 writes.
